I think we're in another transition phase in terms of pricing.  Manufacturing processes seem to be at a point where product tiers like we've become accustomed to seeing simply aren't going to happen anymore. 
The lack of any non-XT cards from AMD, even with the shortages we're dealing with, may well be all that we get for this generation of cards, at least as long as people keep paying for them, which I see as being the case for the foreseeable future. 
As  Steve mentioned in the video, there's no incentive to drop prices. Miners will pay whatever -  <insert your fave epithet here>, and gamers are frankly desperate to an embarrassing degree, so AMD and nVidia can charge whatever they like and people will pay despite you and everyone else warning and imploring them not to. The mining horde basically removes any leverage a regular consumer has to affect pricing because any stock we don't get our hands on will fall to miners, so refusing to pay a premium for cards is basically a thing of the past. 

If it still takes two years to build a new fab and get it running, we're stuck with the trickle of cards we've got until 2023 or 2024, and that's assuming they start now.

Given all that, I believe we need to revise what comprises a good value, as it really only means anything when compared to contemporary cards, and  older(at least two generations back)  cards that people are actually trying to upgrade from. To me that means the 5700XT is kind of irrelevant,  because it wasn't a particularly good value when it debuted, though it's performance has improved with more mature drivers.

As someone not really looking to upgrade the next year, just in it for the love of tech, I guess this can best be summed up with "meh". Unless AMD can feed huge volumes of this thing onto the market, and do so near MSPR for the forseeable future. If that happens, well then at some point we need to reasess the stacks based on the longer term avg prices, that people can actually buy a GPU for - including if placing backorders.

That last bit, placing backorders, is how most people in my region seem to buy them. It's basically a rolling waiting list kind of situation. They place backorders on a credit csrd with big retailers. Then the order sum is reserved - the money isn't actually charged on the card and tied up, before the order actually ships (so no interest before that either, and no waiting for a refund to process if you suddenly need to cancel the order).

This way, they get it near MSRP, but it takes a while; waiting "your turn" while shipments come in and the retailer works its way down the outstanding order lists. If you want to buy something in stock, shipping right away, then you have to pay the scalpers.

If you're waiting for stock to just sit there waiting for you to come" buy now", anywhere near MSRP - then you're keeping yourself perpetually dead last in line to get one, until every other person and company who wants one (or 50) and is willing to place a backorder, all have had their fill, and that "rolling waiting list" is completely empty. And IF that day comes, you'll still be competing with all the others who want to wait and buy like you do.

Only when retailers literally have more units in hand than they have outstanding customer orders to fulfil - will units be listed "In Stock" anywhere near MSRP. Let's just say I'm not putting any money on that happening in 2021.

the 6700 xt feels like a joke. this should be $360-380 at max. the 5700 xt was already overpriced and this barely makes any difference in value. it gets even worse compared to nvidia with the vastly superior feature set for the geforce cards. you already mentioned nvenc, dlss and rtx and i might add openCL performance and non-buggy implementation. im having nothing but issues trying to use radeon gpus with productive software. opencl performance is either really bad (10x worse than nvidia in affinity suite, several months unfixed), broken (took over a year to fix image corruption in capture one) or just not there at all (autocad 3d calls my vega 56 "unsupported gpu"). compared to the 6800XT the 6700XT also loses its edge in efficiency.

the pricing, especially for the lower tier cards, is just ridiculous. at this rate the $200 gpu will be the rx 6010 with 12 CUs and a 32bit memory bus.
